title: YouTuber Hank Green says his AI usage is ‘not healthy’
slides: Hank Green calls his AI usage 'not healthy'—why?
He admits to coding with AI constantly, even at night.
But he deleted his most addictive AI tool completely.
For creators, AI now demands hard usage boundaries.
Set one rule today: no AI after 9 PM.
thread_text:
1. He Deleted His AI Crutch

Hank Green, a creator known for tech enthusiasm, admitted his AI use was 'not healthy'—and then removed his most addictive tool entirely.

2. Even the Addicted See It

He codes with AI constantly, even at night—a habit he compares to an unhealthy dependency. If he can't moderate it, what does that say for the rest of us?

3. The Real Cost for Creators

For writers and makers, AI isn't a one-time boost—it's a constant temptation that erodes focus and sleep. Boundaries aren't optional; they're survival.

4. A Simple Test for You

Check your last 30 days: How many nights did you let AI keep you up? Honest count might surprise you—and that's the first step to reclaiming your time.

5. Set One Rule Tonight

No AI after 9 PM. Just try it for a week. If you find yourself reaching for it anyway, ask why— and maybe delete the app like Hank did.

Then he deleted his favorite AI tool.
Creators need strong boundaries with AI now.
Try: no AI after nine, today.

If a tech-obsessed creator like him can't control the pull, the rest of us are on thin ice. The real cost isn't productivity—it's focus and sleep, the two things your content depends on. 😬

For anyone who writes or makes, this means one thing: boundaries aren't optional anymore, they're survival. You can't out-discipline a tool engineered to keep you hooked.

So here's your concrete step: no AI after 9 PM for one week. Count how many times you reach for it anyway. What number would you see tonight? 🔌
